taxonomy.name: Black hat
taxonomy.meaning: An informal label for malicious or criminal activity for gain, harm, or unauthorized access.
taxonomy.professional_alternative: Threat analysis, malware defense, ransomware recovery, and fraud prevention.

taxonomy.name: White hat
taxonomy.meaning: An informal label for security work performed with explicit authorization and agreed scope.
taxonomy.professional_alternative: Written rules of engagement, evidence-based auditing, remediation, and retesting.

taxonomy.name: Gray hat
taxonomy.meaning: Often describes finding or disclosing flaws without prior permission; good intentions do not establish authorization.
taxonomy.professional_alternative: Use an authorized lab or owner-approved assessment and coordinated disclosure.

taxonomy.name: Green hat
taxonomy.meaning: An inconsistent informal term sometimes used for beginners; it is not a qualification.
taxonomy.professional_alternative: Learn fundamentals, practice on owned synthetic examples, and develop reporting skills.

taxonomy.name: Blue hat
taxonomy.meaning: An ambiguous term used for external security testers in some contexts and revenge-motivated actors in others.
taxonomy.professional_alternative: Account protection, incident response, lawful reporting, and authorized external review.

taxonomy.name: Red hat
taxonomy.meaning: An inconsistent internet label sometimes associated with vigilante retaliation; distinct from an authorized red-team exercise or the software company.
taxonomy.professional_alternative: Defensive detection, incident response, and assessment work with explicit rules of engagement.
